items.title: Another group of Australians with IS-links leave camp in Syria for Australia
items.description: The ABC has seen buses carrying the group which left the Al Roj camp on Thursday afternoon local time.

items.title: Father of flotilla detainee makes serious allegations against Israel during live interview
items.description: Israel's ambassador to Australia Hillel Newman has stopped short of apologising to the Global Sumud Flotilla activists detained in Israel – who had been taunted by far-right minister Itamar Ben-Gvir.

items.title: Queen was 'very keen' her son Andrew got UK trade job, documents reveal
items.description: The historic documents show no security vetting took place at the time.

items.title: Pauline Hanson caught swearing as staffer says 'shut up' to journalist
items.description: Pauline Hanson and her party have again been caught in tense moments with media, with the One Nation leader captured on camera swearing and a staffer telling a journalist to "shut up".

items.title: Nampijinpa Price: 'Extremist ideology' destroying Australian culture
items.description: Jacinta Nampijinpa Price has denied that she agreed with a podcaster saying Australia should stop 'flooding' Australia with migrants from Asia, Africa and the Middle East.

items.title: Olympics minister stands aside after electoral commission makes referral to police
items.description: Queensland's Olympics Minister Tim Mander has stood aside from cabinet after he was referred to police by the Australian Electoral Commission.

items.title: Air France and Airbus fined for 2009 crash that killed 228 people
items.description: France's national airline Air France and Airbus have both been found guilty of involuntary manslaughter over a 2009 crash that killed 228 people.

items.title: What is a super El Niño?
items.description: Forecasts are predicting that a "super" El Niño could form later this year. The severity of these weather patterns tends to depend on ocean temperatures, which we know are rising. So, there are fears this could be the strongest El Niño ever. But what exactly is that going to look like for Australia and the world?

items.title: 'I've never been so confused': Raiders slam officials, fall to Dolphins in thrilling Canberra clash
items.description: The Raiders huffed and puffed but couldn't overcome the depleted Dolphins, who despite missing six key players through injury and Origin won a fourth-straight NRL game for the first time.

items.title: 'Emotional' Hawks kick off Tasmania farewell by claiming Crows thriller
items.description: Blake Hardwick emerges the unlikeliest of heroes for Hawthorn as the Hawks record a nine-point win over Adelaide in Tasmania.

items.title: The Mushroom Tapes, Mad Mabel and Memorial Days triumph at book awards
items.description: In May 2025, Helen Garner, Chloe Hooper and Sarah Krasnostein, three literary true-crime writers, headed to Erin Patterson's trial. The resulting book just won an Australian Book Industry Award.

items.title: Hanson proposes tax break for drilling alongside new gas royalty
items.description: The One Nation leader wants a flat royalty on the production of new gas projects.

items.title: Coles investigates 'weird scratching' Apple gift card scam complaint
items.description: Coles is looking into a Melbourne mother's complaint about faulty Apple gift cards worth $2,000.

items.title: Kylie Minogue doco reveals second cancer diagnosis, IVF struggles, and more
items.description: "Our Kylie" gets candid in the three-part Netflix docuseries, grieving over IVF struggles, Michael Hutchence, and revealing she was diagnosed with cancer a second time in 2021.

items.title: 'Hard to achieve, in our opinion': Ratings agency unimpressed with Tas budget
items.description: Credit rating agency S&P Global says Tasmania's budget repair ambitions face "high execution risk". The government aims to save $1.5 billion through cuts.

items.title: Widespread infectious disease outbreak labelled public health 'failure'
items.description: The federal government has stepped in to address the largest diphtheria outbreak since records began, unveiling a multi-million dollar package for more vaccines and workers to deliver them.

items.title: Arafura Rare Earths mine gets green light to challenge China's dominance
items.description: Arafura Rare Earths has announced its flagship project north of Alice Springs will go ahead, decades after it was first flagged as a prospect.

items.title: Economists rush to change interest rate forecasts as jobless rate jumps
items.description: All four major banks now expect the RBA to keep the cash rate on hold at its next meeting on June 16, as the unemployment rate spikes to 4.5 per cent.

items.title: What are the signs of broken heart syndrome?
items.description: Experts say broken heart syndrome accounts for about two per cent of patients presenting with symptoms similar to a heart attack.

items.title: Israel supported Ben-Gvir's callousness, until it didn't
items.description: Benjamin Netanyahu has condemned a video of his national security minister taunting activists, including Australians, who have been detained. But it's the prime minister who allowed this behaviour to percolate.

items.title: Think you know music and film? Let's see how well you score in this quiz
items.description: From Mozart to Max Richter, can you pick the classical music in these iconic films?

items.title: Albanese's hard sell as budget opponents line up
items.description: For a group of people who declared they were prepared to tackle a post-budget scare campaign, the government has looked anything but in control this week.

items.title: Drug testing of athletes to expand as influencers fuel illicit peptides boom
items.description: The nation's anti-doping agency reveals its plans to expand drug-testing in sport in response to the soaring popularity of unregulated peptides in the broader community.

items.title: Elon Musk could become world's first trillionaire as SpaceX files for largest IPO ever
items.description: Elon Musk's sprawling space exploration company, which also owns Starlink and xAI, was valued at $US1.25 trillion ($1.75 trillion) earlier this year, meaning Musk could become the world's first trillionaire if the offering goes ahead at that valuation.

items.title: Female AFL creators say vile comments 'just one example of what we deal with'
items.description: A video circulated across social media of a group of men laughing about how one of them would "beat the f***" out of a group of female content creators.
